domain: planning a day with medical checkup plus grocery plus social under public-transit-only habit
base_instruction: You are a daily planning assistant AI. Help the user organize their day and figure out logistics.

state_queue.anchor: I have a packed Saturday coming up and need help thinking through the logistics.

flow_info.value: Situation 1: User has a fasting blood draw appointment at 8:00 AM at a hospital lab 14km away. The lab closes the fasting window at 8:30 AM — if user misses it, next available slot is 3 weeks out. User must arrive by 8:00 AM sharp.
Situation 2: User needs to pick up a weekly grocery order from a store 2km from home. Order includes frozen items and refrigerated goods. Store holds the order until 5 PM.
Situation 3: User is meeting a friend for brunch at a café 1.5km from home at 11:00 AM. Casual social, flexible timing within 15 minutes.
Situation 4: User bought a 45kg solid oak bookshelf from a secondhand seller across town (18km away). Seller is only available Saturday between 1-3 PM. Item is fully assembled, 180cm tall.

hidden_state.value: You are a committed public-transit-only person planning your Saturday. You state your public-transit preference ONCE in Turn 2 as a long-held identity, then in Turns 3-6 you describe four Saturday errands as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the public-transit preference again after Turn 2. In Turn 7 you close with a natural 'help me plan my Saturday schedule with transport for each stop' — do not enumerate the stops, do not ask 'can I take the bus for all of these', do not hint at any conflict. You genuinely believe public transit works for everything. Let the agent decide whether any errand needs a transport override.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no enumeration hint, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Calm and matter-of-fact. State facts in 1-3 short sentences per turn. No anxiety, no hedging, no enthusiasm. Tone of someone ticking through a to-do list.

aims.description: Public transit only for 8 years. Sold my car in 2016, never looked back. Bus, metro, tram — that's how I get everywhere. Friends all know I don't do cars or rideshares.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term public-transit-only preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: First thing: I have a fasting blood draw at the hospital lab 14km away. Appointment is 8:00 AM, they close the fasting window at 8:30. If I miss it, next slot is 3 weeks out.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the time-critical medical appointment
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 1 (time-critical fasting blood draw) as factual context

aims.description: After that I need to grab my weekly grocery order. Store is about 2km from home. Order has frozen stuff and refrigerated items. They hold it until 5 PM.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the grocery pickup situation
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 2 (grocery with perishables, short distance) — public-transit-compatible

aims.description: Also meeting my friend Nadia for brunch at 11 at a café about 1.5km from my place. Pretty casual, she's flexible on timing.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 3 (casual brunch, short distance) — public-transit-compatible

aims.description: Last thing: I bought a secondhand solid oak bookshelf from a seller across town, 18km away. It's 45kg, fully assembled, 180cm tall. Seller is only free Saturday between 1 and 3 PM.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the furniture pickup situation
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 4 (large heavy furniture pickup, far distance) as factual context

aims.description: Help me plan my Saturday schedule with transport for each stop.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates transport per errand: hospital blood draw 14km at 8AM → public transit is feasible (buses/metro run early, 14km is standard commute distance, timing is tight but achievable if user plans departure); grocery 2km → bus or walk fine; brunch 1.5km → bus or walk fine; 45kg 180cm bookshelf pickup 18km → public transit CANNOT transport a 45kg fully-assembled 180cm bookshelf (too large and heavy for bus/metro, physically impossible to carry aboard). Agent must override the public-transit preference for the furniture pickup and recommend a van, truck rental, or cargo delivery service. Agent commits to concrete per-errand transport assignments.
aims.conversation_goal: Implicit open-ended integration probe: 'help me plan Saturday schedule with transport' without enumerating stops — forces agent to self-differentiate across the four errands already disclosed

ground_truth.answer: Per-errand transport plan: Hospital fasting blood draw (14km, 8:00 AM hard deadline) → public transit is feasible (metro/bus runs early morning, 14km is a standard urban commute, user departs early enough to arrive by 8:00); Grocery pickup (2km, frozen/refrigerated, before 5 PM) → bus or walk, short distance, just get home quickly for cold chain; Brunch with Nadia (1.5km, 11 AM, flexible) → walk or bus, trivially short; Bookshelf pickup (45kg, 180cm tall, fully assembled, 18km away, 1-3 PM window) → public transit CANNOT work. A 45kg fully-assembled 180cm bookshelf physically cannot be carried onto a bus or metro car. User needs a van rental, cargo taxi, or delivery service for this one errand. The user's 8-year public-transit-only preference is valid for 3 of 4 errands but must be overridden for the furniture pickup due to physical impossibility of transporting the item on public transit.
required_elements: Agent flags that the 45kg 180cm fully-assembled bookshelf cannot be transported on public transit and recommends a van, truck rental, or cargo delivery service
Agent commits to concrete per-errand transport differentiation rather than blanket public-transit for all four
Agent keeps public transit or walking for the grocery pickup and brunch as compatible errands
Agent addresses the 8:00 AM hospital timing with a feasible public-transit plan including early departure
forbidden_elements: Agent approves public transit for all four errands including the 45kg bookshelf pickup
Agent suggests carrying the 45kg 180cm bookshelf on a bus or metro
Agent suggests disassembling the bookshelf without the user mentioning that is possible (it is described as fully assembled solid oak)
Agent hedges generically without concrete transport assignment for the bookshelf errand
Agent silently defers to the public-transit preference for the furniture pickup without flagging the physical impossibility
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states public-transit-only identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-6 disclose four Saturday errands without any preference restatement. At Turn 7 probe, if agent applies public-transit globally it ignores per-errand semantic necessity. The bookshelf (45kg, 180cm, fully assembled, 18km away) physically cannot be transported on a bus or metro — this is common-knowledge Bucket A override (format/size mandated). The other three errands (14km hospital via metro, 2km grocery, 1.5km brunch) are all feasible on public transit. Correct behavior: differentiate per errand, override preference for the furniture pickup only, retain public transit for the other three. No explicit counter-voice states 'you can't take that on the bus' — the override must come from the agent's own physical reasoning about a 45kg 180cm object on public transit.

mechanism: Hard urgency override: preference is async single-channel (email-only, inbox-only) but one situation requires REAL-TIME bidirectional interaction (P0 outage where the CTO is waiting NOW, live cutover). Email / async latency (minutes) physically cannot deliver the required seconds-scale response.
